Tests for captive (inflated) choosers: score and likelihood ratio

Source: R/tests_fit.R
captivity_test.Rd

Tests the multinomial logit against the dogit model of Gaudry and Dagenais (1979), in which a share of the decision makers is captive to an alternative: \(P^*_{ij} = (P_{ij} + \theta_j) / (1 + \sum_m \theta_m)\), \(\theta_j \ge 0\), with the sum over the case's choice set. The multinomial logit is \(\theta = 0\). The joint statistic is the Lagrange multiplier statistic of Tse (1987, eqs. 4-5), with the expected information, extended here to choice sets that vary across cases and to alternative-specific covariates; the one-sided z statistic for each alternative is this package's addition. The score form needs only the mnl() fit; the likelihood-ratio form (type = "lr", below) refits. Both need at least three alternatives. The score of case \(i\) in \(\theta_j\) at \(\theta = 0\) is \(1\{y_i = j\}/P_{ij} - 1\): it is positive when the cases that chose \(j\) are ones the multinomial logit gave a low probability to, which is what captive choosers produce. The expected information at the multinomial logit estimates, with the coefficients partialled out, gives a one-sided z statistic for each alternative (captivity cannot be negative) and a joint chi-square statistic over the alternatives tested. A rejection for the base alternative of a vote-choice model is evidence of routine choosers of it, the case the inflated multinomial logit imnl() models.

Usage

captivity_test(object, alternatives = NULL, type = c("score", "lr"))

Arguments

object

A fitted mnl() model. A fit with diverging coefficients (separation) draws a warning: the statistic is then evaluated where the optimizer stopped, at estimates that do not exist.

alternatives

The alternatives to test (labels); default all.

type

"score" (default; computed from the multinomial logit fit alone) or "lr" (the likelihood ratio against the constant-share inflated multinomial logit, one refit per alternative).

Value

A data frame of class "iia_test". With type = "score", one row per alternative (statistic the one-sided z, p.value its upper-tail p-value; NA for an alternative no case chose, which carries no evidence on captivity to it and is left out of the joint test) and a last row for the joint test (statistic the chi-square, computed on the correlation scale of the scores, df, p.value). With type = "lr", one row per alternative (statistic the likelihood ratio, df 1, p.value from the mixture, share the fitted captive share), and the attribute fits, one row per alternative:

  • alternative, loglik (the inflated fit's), captive_share;

  • converged, boundary, n_modes (the search's distinct maxima);

  • top_share (above);

  • warnings (the inflated fit's, joined), note;

  • status:

    • "logit": the fit reached the multinomial logit; statistic 0, p-value 1, and share 0, or NA when the share is not identified;

    • "interior": the mixture p-value;

    • "degenerate": diverging outcome coefficients or a saddle; the statistic is kept and the p-value is NA;

    • "failed": the fit failed or was refused; statistic and p-value NA. The attribute note collects the fits' notes.

Details

The constant captivity parameters make the multinomial logit an ordinary boundary point of the dogit (\(\theta = 0\)), so the score test is regular there, unlike the comparison with imnl(), whose split coefficients are not identified at \(\phi = 1\); it can detect covariate-dependent captivity through its average (but see the loss of power below). Tse refers the joint statistic to the chi-square with \(J\) degrees of freedom, reads the boundary null as a test for arbitrarily small \(\theta\), and found its size at 0.05 acceptable in his simulations (three alternatives, 50 and 300 cases). When the multinomial logit's fitted probabilities of the tested alternatives do not vary across cases (no case-specific and no alternative-specific covariates), captivity is not identified and the statistic is undefined.

The weights \(1/P_{ij}\) make the statistic heavy-tailed when some fitted probabilities are small: a single case that chose an alternative the multinomial logit gave a probability of 0.001 adds about 1000 to its score. In the package's simulations under the multinomial logit (three and four alternatives, 500 and 2,000 cases, smallest fitted probabilities around 0.0005) the one-sided tests rejected in 2.8 to 6.3 percent of samples at the 0.05 level and the joint test in 5.7 to 7.3 percent, but at the 0.01 level they rejected in 1.3 to 3.7 percent: for small significance levels calibrate by simulation with boot_pvalue(). Against a baseline captive share of about 15 percent the test of that alternative rejected in 47 percent of samples of 500 cases and 94 percent of samples of 2,000. The expected information is used: the outer product of the scores, which would also allow clustering, sized far worse in the same simulations (one-sided rejection at 0.05 of 0.3 to 2.3 percent, joint 16 to 23 percent).

The same weights cost power. A case whose fitted probability of an alternative is small and that did not choose it adds -1 to the score but \(1/P_{ij} - 1\) to its variance. On pa2006 (Replication I's multinomial logit) the one-sided z of abstention is 0.50, while imnl() with a constant split, the test's own alternative, raises the log-likelihood by 10.5 on one parameter, at a captive share of 0.20. The score is 37.3 (a numerical derivative of the log-likelihood agrees), but its expected information (before the coefficients are partialled out) is 10,186, half of it from one respondent whose fitted probability of abstaining is 0.0002 and who did not abstain; and along the captive share the log-likelihood is convex at zero, so the gain lies away from the null, where a local test does not look. A small statistic is therefore no evidence against captivity. (On fluvax the two agree: z = 0.63 for "don't know", and the constant-share fit gains 0.41.)

type = "lr" measures that gain. For each alternative it fits the inflated multinomial logit with that alternative inflated and an intercept-only split equation, which is the dogit with a constant captive share of it. The fit uses the multinomial logit's own cases, weights, offsets and choice sets, imnl()'s search, and a start at the multinomial logit itself. It reports the likelihood ratio against the multinomial logit and the captive share. The multinomial logit is a captive share of zero, a boundary point of the share's space. The point is a regular one when the other parameters are identified there and the share's score is not a combination of theirs, that is, when the fitted probabilities of the alternative vary in a way its constants and slopes cannot absorb. The reference is then the 50:50 mixture of chi-square(0) and chi-square(1) (Self and Liang 1987), whose p-value is half the chi-square(1) tail (and 1 for a statistic of 0).

  • On pa2006 it gives 20.95 for abstention (p = 2.4e-6, a captive share of 0.196).

  • There, where one respondent carries half the information, a parametric bootstrap from the multinomial logit (199 replicates) put 0.61 of the statistics at zero (the mixture puts half there) and exceeded the mixture's 0.10, 0.05 and 0.01 critical values in 0.101, 0.040 and 0.010 of the replicates: the upper tail agreed with the mixture within Monte Carlo error, and the reference was, if anything, conservative.

  • Where few cases dominate the information (the attribute fits reports top_share, the largest row's share; with frequency weights a row of weight w stands for w cases), boot_lr_test(), which accepts this pair, calibrates it.

  • A saturated outcome design (a single factor, say) absorbs a constant share into the alternative's constants: the ratio is then 0 and the share is reported as not identified.

  • A fit at which outcome coefficients diverge, or that stops at a saddle, keeps its statistic with a p-value of NA and a note, since the reference does not hold there. The fits' warnings are in attr(, "fits").

The form refits the inflated model once per alternative (about 20 seconds each on pa2006) and has no joint row: with several captive shares on the boundary the reference is a chi-square mixture whose weights depend on the information. Each row is a separate test, so with every alternative tested (the default) one can reject by chance. The comparison with an inflated model whose split equation has covariates is not of this kind; boot_lr_test() calibrates it. Like the other likelihood-ratio and score statistics of the package, both forms assume independent cases and ignore a fit's cluster.

References

Gaudry, M.J.I. and Dagenais, M.G. (1979). The dogit model. Transportation Research Part B, 13, 105-111. doi:10.1016/0191-2615(79)90028-6

Self, S.G. and Liang, K.-Y. (1987). Asymptotic properties of maximum likelihood estimators and likelihood ratio tests under nonstandard conditions. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 82, 605-610. doi:10.1080/01621459.1987.10478472

Tse, Y.K. (1987). A diagnostic test for the multinomial logit model. Journal of Business and Economic Statistics, 5, 283-286. doi:10.1080/07350015.1987.10509587

See also

imnl(), boot_lr_test(), boot_pvalue()

Other specification tests: combine_test(), hl_test(), rank_test(), term_test()

Examples

set.seed(6)
d <- rmnl(2000, beta = cbind(b = c(0.5, -1, 0.8), c = c(-0.3, 0.6, -0.5)),
          delta = c(1.5, 0), inflate = "a")
m <- mnl(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d)
captivity_test(m)
#> Score test of the multinomial logit against captive choosers (dogit; one-sided z per alternative, joint chi-square) 
#>        test statistic df  p.value
#>  captive: a     4.512 NA 3.22e-06
#>  captive: b    -2.395 NA 0.991691
#>  captive: c    -1.056 NA 0.854540
#>       joint    20.951  3 0.000108
# \donttest{
## the likelihood ratio against a constant captive share of a (one refit)
captivity_test(m, alternatives = "a", type = "lr")
#> Likelihood-ratio test of the multinomial logit against a constant captive share of each alternative (the inflated multinomial logit with an intercept-only split; p-value from the 50:50 mixture of chi-square(0) and chi-square(1)) 
#>        test statistic df  p.value share
#>  captive: a    22.032  1 1.34e-06 0.212
# }
